claude.sample_unit: validation images (CBIS-DDSM; external: CMMD 1032, DMID 509, MIAS 322)

links.outcome: AUC drop at external sites/sensors versus in-distribution
links.effect: Every model lost 0.165 to 0.320 AUC points at transfer; ResNet-50 fell from 0.867 to 0.568 on CMMD, 0.547 on DMID, 0.630 on MIAS; sensitivity at 95% specificity fell from 0.31-0.47 to 0.11-0.22.
links.quote: Every model, at every target population, lost more than 0.165 AUC points relative to its in-distribution performance, and sensitivity at 95% specificity dropped from 0.31 to 0.47 in-distribution to 0.11 to 0.22 across the three external targets.

links.outcome: Performance of internally validated models on external unrepresentative cohorts
links.effect: In-distribution AUC 0.867 for ResNet-50 collapsed to 0.547-0.630 on external cohorts; all models lost 0.165-0.320 AUC.
links.quote: AUC measured on the training population is not a reliable proxy for in-clinic performance.

links.outcome: Performance and calibration on non-local data versus source data
links.effect: Sensitivity at 95% specificity fell to 0.107 for ResNet-50 on DMID; ECE rose from 0.055 in-distribution to 0.186-0.253 at transfer targets.
links.quote: Mammography AI products approved in one national context cannot be safely deployed in another without subgroup-stratified external validation and local recalibration.

links.outcome: ECE change from temperature scaling fitted on source data applied to transfer targets
links.effect: Temperature scaling gave modest ECE improvements (Δ −0.009 to −0.049); worst transfer cells remained at ECE 0.30 or higher.
links.quote: Even after recalibration, the worst transfer cells remain at ECE 0.30 or higher, well above any clinically acceptable level.

links.outcome: Dataset shift across sensor, prevalence, label source, and demographics
links.effect: Cohorts differed in detector, prevalence (40%/70%/23%/16%), labels, demographics; intensity distributions differed (mean 0.40, 0.64, 0.47); large transfer AUC drops.
links.quote: The visible distributional differences across these three cohorts support, but do not by themselves prove, a sensor-shift contribution to the cross-population transfer drops in Table 5 .

links.outcome: AUC across BI-RADS density subgroups on CBIS-DDSM
links.effect: ResNet-50 D1 0.912 to D4 0.842; Mammo-FM D4 0.870 vs ResNet-50 0.842 (n=140, CIs overlap); all models lose AUC as density increases.
links.quote: Second, all models lose AUC points as tissue density increases, which matches the clinical expectation.

links.outcome: Aggregate AUC masking subgroup performance differences
links.effect: Aggregate AUC favored ResNet-50 (0.867 vs 0.846) while Mammo-FM led in D4 (0.870 vs 0.842); subgroup AUCs varied by density for all models.
links.quote: The per-subgroup analysis in Table 4 shows that aggregate AUC obscures the cells where domain-specific pretraining actually helps.

links.outcome: Foundation models compared to simpler ResNet-50 baseline on same data
links.effect: ResNet-50 (AUC 0.867) outperformed Mammo-CLIP (0.847), Mammo-FM (0.846), DINOv2 (0.813), Rad-DINO (0.703); all gaps p_adj<0.05.
links.quote: No foundation model beats the ResNet-50 baseline, and the gaps are statistically significant once predictions are stacked across seeds and run through a paired DeLong test.

links.outcome: Effect of density-aware loss mitigation on AUC and calibration
links.effect: Density-aware focal loss reduced AUC by 0.031-0.061 and doubled ECE (0.055 to 0.104-0.116) at every weight.
links.quote: Adding the density-aware auxiliary loss degraded performance on every weight setting tested.

links.outcome: Calibration deterioration hidden by discrimination metrics at transfer
links.effect: Mammo-CLIP ECE on CMMD reached 0.403 and DINOv2 on MIAS 0.446, versus 0.055-0.105 in-distribution.
links.quote: Mammo-CLIP’s ECE on CMMD reaches 0.403, meaning its predicted probabilities are on average 40 percentage points off from the actual prevalence after distribution shift.

unlisted_practices: Density-aware focal loss for subgroup-conditioned training
Per-seed Stouffer meta-analysis for significance testing

openai.country: United States; China; India; United Kingdom

links.outcome: External validation AUC and sensitivity
links.effect: Every model lost >0.165 AUC; sensitivity at 95% specificity dropped from 0.31–0.47 in-distribution to 0.11–0.22 externally.
links.quote: Every model, at every target population, lost more than 0.165 AUC points relative to its in-distribution performance, and sensitivity at 95% specificity dropped from 0.31 to 0.47 in-distribution to 0.11 to 0.22 across the three external targets.

links.outcome: Backbone AUC versus simpler baseline
links.effect: ResNet-50 AUC 0.867; Mammo-CLIP 0.847, Mammo-FM 0.846, DINOv2 0.813, Rad-DINO 0.703; all gaps p_adj<0.05.
links.quote: No foundation model beats the ResNet-50 baseline, and the gaps are statistically significant once predictions are stacked across seeds and run through a paired DeLong test.

links.outcome: Development-to-target dataset shift
links.effect: External cohorts differed in detector, prevalence, label source, and demographics; transfer AUC drops were 0.165–0.320.
links.quote: The three external evaluation cohorts differ from CBIS-DDSM along at least four axes simultaneously: X-ray detector technology, malignancy prevalence, label source, and patient demographics (see Section 5.4 ).

links.outcome: AUC by external cohort and sensor
links.effect: Across CMMD, DMID, and MIAS, all 12 model-target AUC drops were negative, −0.165 to −0.320.
links.quote: All 12 transfer cells show negative drops between −0.165 and −0.320.

links.outcome: Dense-breast subgroup performance
links.effect: Aggregate ResNet-50 led Mammo-FM 0.867 vs 0.846, but D4 subgroup reversed direction: Mammo-FM 0.870 vs ResNet-50 0.842; CIs overlapped.
links.quote: At the subgroup level, Mammo-FM outperforms ResNet-50 in the extremely dense bin (D4 AUC 0.870 vs. 0.842), although the 95% CIs of the two models overlap heavily at the D4 sample size of n = 140, so this cell should be interpreted as a directional signal worth following up rather than a statistically supported advantage.

links.outcome: Calibration under distribution shift
links.effect: Mammo-CLIP ECE on CMMD 0.403; DINOv2 ECE on MIAS 0.446; after temperature scaling, worst cells remained ECE ≥0.30.
links.quote: Mammo-CLIP’s ECE on CMMD reaches 0.403, meaning its predicted probabilities are on average 40 percentage points off from the actual prevalence after distribution shift.

unlisted_practices: Density-aware focal loss conditioned on BI-RADS density bin
Source-fitted temperature scaling recalibration applied to external cohorts

links.quote: At transfer, every model lost 0.165 to 0.320 AUC points relative to in-distribution performance, with sensitivity at 95% specificity collapsing from 0.31 to 0.47 in-distribution to 0.11 to 0.22 across the three external targets.

links.outcome: in-distribution discrimination of foundation models versus simpler ResNet-50 baseline

screen.practice: local recalibration (temperature scaling) and external validation before deployment
screen.reason: Empirical multi-dataset benchmark testing cross-sensor and cross-population generalization across four countries, specifically testing post hoc recalibration (temperature scaling) and assessing requirements for local validation prior to deployment.

primary.practice: post hoc recalibration and local external validation across sensors/populations
